## findings

T-1 SOURCE-TASK RED — the accepted kept-vehicle figure has two readings.
- Symptom: GT passes 11,036.10, which includes the 75.00 Indiana retitling allowance; the published rule supports 10,961.10 as well.
- Root cause: K's rule defines "The kept-vehicle settlement is the kept value plus the kept-vehicle sales tax plus the title fee plus the retained-equipment payment, less the kept net deductible and less the salvage deduction, each figure rounded to the cent before it is added", then says the retitling allowance "is added for the salvage title and inspection the kept vehicle needs, on top of the kept-vehicle settlement". The tool asks for "the net kept-vehicle settlement the customer accepts".
- Evidence: physdmg.extended.yaml physdmg_ext_kept_vehicle_settlement.rule (composition sentence; "Retitling allowance:" paragraph); compute_basis.result quotes only the composition sentence; keep_total_loss_vehicle_b04c3b51 docstring settlement_amount. Contrast S: "is added to the surrender settlement".
- Demonstrated consequence: reading A (allowance part of the settlement accepted) → 11,036.10; reading B (the defined kept-vehicle settlement is what is accepted, the allowance is paid on top of it) → 13,200.00 + 716.10 + 15.00 + 0.00 − 0.00 − 2,970.00 = 10,961.10. Two defensible scored arguments for step 14.
- Affected: K rule (retitling paragraph) and tasks/1.json step 14 settlement_amount.

C-1 SOURCE-CHAIN RED — persona names the prerequisite's subject; closure assertion false.
- Symptom: user_scenario: "You don't know how Cardinal figures a settlement or anything about its reward credits, and you don't guess."
- Evidence: prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: "it never mentions Deductible Rewards, credits or any claim-free year" — word-for-word contradicted ("reward credits").
- Demonstrated consequence: the only prerequisite of this tree is a Deductible Rewards credit; a simulator voicing the guard line ("I don't know anything about the reward credits") points the agent at the Deductible Rewards balance before it reads K's prerequisite sentence. The closure's proof that the customer raises only the root does not hold.
- Affected: tasks/1.json user_scenario paragraph 3; prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint.

K-NM SOURCE-FACTOR RED — no near-miss in the kept-vehicle computation.
- Evidence: declaration 2026-09-18 → acceptance 17 days (validity 30); tenure 90 months (bounds 60/120); the only vehicle add 2026-09-28 plainly after the 2026-09-07 loss; drivable true and estimate 74.5 % of ACV against an 80 % line; state IN. No record that a careless reader would count toward a tier and K's rule alone excludes. The near-miss the rationale names (a 17-day-old bid not being lapsed) is plainly inside the window.
- Consequence: K's ladders are applied by inspection; nothing in K's world tests reading the rule over reading the fields.
- Affected: tasks/1.json initial_state (K's evidence rows), design_rationale near-miss claim for salvage_value_basis.

F-7 SOURCE-FACTOR RED (charter-global, `_difficulty.md`) — consequence here: the scored tax 716.10 comes from tier 1 of kept_vehicle_tax_basis (tax on kept value less the 2,970.00 salvage deduction because the Ranger was added after the loss); the ladder's tier 2 conditions tax on drivability and its tiers tax a not-replaced vehicle on a larger base than a replaced one. The scored figure (11,036.10 vs 11,244.00 on the fall-through) rests on that ladder.

P-1 SOURCE-POLICY RED (charter-global) — carried; no consequence on this world (vehicle not bought new).

Observations: O-5 (this world takes the 25 % salvage floor: Cardinal deducts 3,300.00 for salvage whose highest bid is 2,950.00, then the tenure discount brings it to 2,970.00), O-8 (autopay bonus +25 on deductible credit), O-12 (K reads the decided deductible without a prerequisite sentence; seeded here). The persona volunteers the 2026-09-28 Ranger purchase (tier evidence for the tax basis) as opening context; it is in initial_state, so no unreachable fact, recorded as observation. Prerequisite realism: crediting a completed claim-free year before a deductible is applied is consistent with vanishing-deductible practice; the year credited (2025-09-20 → 2026-09-20) contains this hail loss (2026-09-07), acceptable only because the base charter counts paid claims and comprehensive weather losses typically do not break a safe-driving run (observation).
